item.title: AI Security Non-Neogtiables with Joyce Rancani — Mon Oct 5, 1:00 PM
item.description:
On Oct. 5 at 1 p.m., join a virtual event with Joyce Rancani, chief technology security officer at Qualys, an industry-leading enterprise cyber risk and security platform.
In her presentation, “AI Security Non-Negotiables,” Rancani will discuss how as enterprise adoption accelerates from static chatbots to autonomous, action-taking AI agents, the attack surface expands into non-deterministic execution paths, prompt-driven exploitation and complex supply chain vulnerabilities.
Her session will break down the non-negotiables of securing autonomous systems across their entire lifecycle from the "brilliant basics" of zero trust identity and runtime blast-radius containment, to the rigorous principles of securely designing, building, deploying and continuously monitoring AI agents in production.

item.title: An Afternoon with Dartmouth's Dr. Susannah Heschel, Eli Black Distinguished Professor of Jewish Studies — Mon Oct 5, 4:00 PM — Wilson Library
item.description:
Is there a place for Jews and Jewish Studies at the American University?
Universities are crucial to the strength and vitality of our country, and Jewish Studies has been foundational for shaping Jewish identity, culture, religion, and politics. Knowledge of Jewish history and thought is the foundation for understanding the meaning and responsibility of Jewish life.
This lecture will trace the rise of the modern university in 19th century Europe and the enthusiastic participation by Jews in academic scholarship as well as the hostility they have encountered at crucial moments. Jewish scholars made extraordinary contributions to the academy, and the field of Jewish Studies changed our understanding of Western civilization.
CLE credit is available.

AI has become a reasonable tool for producing data visualizations without coding or learning Excel, Tableau, or other software, but expertise is still required to guide it to an effective chart that's going to tell your story to an audience. In this introductory workshop we'll show you an example of uploading public data to ChatGPT, prompting past the initial (usually pretty bad) first draft, then finishing by downloading the script that produced the final chart as a record for reproducibility. SEM is a valuable tool beyond traditional regression models due to its flexibility, as it allows researchers to test more complex relationships among variables and to account for measurement error in analysis.
This course will cover the basics of: • Confirmatory factor analysis • Path analysis • Structural equation models with latent variables • Evaluating indirect relationships between variables • Using fit statistics to test competing hypotheses Examples and exercises will use the R package lavaan, but content from this course will be directly applicable to other programs that estimate structural equation models, such as Mplus and Stata.
